newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to scrap tax exemption on Treasury paper.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to scrap tax exemption on Treasury paper.

text.p: Vietnam has withdrawn tax exemption on interest income from Treasury bonds and bills earned by institutions, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.
The official said individuals holding treasury stock would continue to be exempted from tax, but only temporarily.
The new ruling came into effect on November 21. Interest income on paper issued before that date which is held by either an individual or an institution will not be subject to tax.
At present, institutions pay tax on bank deposit interest, but not on interest earned from government debt issues.

The official declined to give the tax rate which would be levied on interest income from treasury paper and the tax department declined to comment. However, foreign bankers in Hanoi said the rate would probably be between 25 and 45 percent.
One banker said the decision looked certain to increase upward pressure on interest rate bids at treasury paper auctions as investors seek compensation for the new tax.
Some 900 billion dong ($81.14 million) worth of treasury bills and notes have been allocated to domestic and foreign institutions at auctions this year.
